references.text: Later in the same chapter it is confirmed that Barabbas was released – he who had been thrown into prison for rebellion and murder ([ref:Luk 23:25|Luke 23:25]).
Mark gives a parallel account of Barabbas and describes him as one who was imprisoned with rebels, those who had committed murders during the uprising ([ref:Mark 15:7|Mark 15:7]).
John describes Barabbas as a robber and tells how the crowd chose him instead of Jesus ([ref:Joh 18:40|John 18:40]).
Matthew's parallel account refers to Barabbas as a notorious prisoner ([ref:Matt 27:16|Matthew 27:16]).
Peter later speaks to the people and points out that they denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be set free ([ref:Apg 3:14|Acts 3:14]).
